---
title: "Recommended packages"
---

This page describes how the translations of the [recommended packages](https://translate.rx.studio/projects/the-r-project-recommended-packages/#components) contributed on Weblate are sent upstream.

Unlike base R, these translations are not part of the [quarterly patch for R Core](Weblate-server.qmd#quarterly-patch-for-r-core).
Each package has its own maintainer and repository, so the contributions need to be sent to each one separately, as a pull request or as a patch.
This process needs admin access to Weblate and, for some steps, SSH access to the Weblate server.

## Tracking

For each round of contributions, open an issue in the [translations repository](https://github.com/r-devel/translations/issues) for tracking, listing the status of each package.
See, for example, [r-devel/translations#68](https://github.com/r-devel/translations/issues/68).

## First steps (for all packages) {#first-steps}

These steps are the same for every package, whatever the way the translations are sent upstream (pull request or patch).
For each package you are going to send upstream:

1. Lock the package's components (e.g. both the `C` and `R` files components), so no new translations are added while the contribution is being reviewed upstream.

This can be done in the Weblate interface, on each component's page ("Operations" > "Repository maintenance" > "Lock").

Alternatively, use the CLI inside the Docker container (see the [Weblate server page](Weblate-server.qmd#git-rebase-conflicts) on how to attach it), once for each component:

```sh
weblate lock_translation the-r-project-recommended-packages/NAME-OF-THE-COMPONENT
```

2. Check that there are no pending changes to commit in the components ("Operations" > "Repository maintenance").
If there are, click "Commit".
Weblate keeps new translations in its database and commits them to the component's repository from time to time.

3. SSH to the Weblate server and make a backup of the package's Git repository (outside the Docker container).

When a package has both `C` and `R` files components, only one of them has its own repository (the other is linked to it), so this is the one to back up.
For the packages hosted on GitHub or Codeberg, this is the `R` files component (e.g. `rpart-r-files`).
The packages hosted on the R-project SVN all share the repository of the `kernsmooth-r-files` component.

First, check that the folder with this name exists on the server:

```sh
sudo ls /var/lib/docker/volumes/weblate-docker_weblate-data/_data/vcs/the-r-project-recommended-packages/
```

The output should be similar to this:

```
class-r-files       lattice-r-files  matrix-r-files  rpart-r-files
kernsmooth-r-files  mass-r-files     nnet-r-files    spatial-r-files
```

Create the backup, replacing `NAME-OF-THE-COMPONENT` (twice) with the folder name from the output above (e.g. `rpart-r-files`):

```sh
sudo tar -zcvf /root/NAME-OF-THE-COMPONENT-repo-$(date '+%Y-%m-%d').tar.gz \
  /var/lib/docker/volumes/weblate-docker_weblate-data/_data/vcs/the-r-project-recommended-packages/NAME-OF-THE-COMPONENT
```

Then check that the backup file is listed, with today's date:

```sh
sudo ls -lh /root/
```

## Getting and sending the translations

How to get the translations from Weblate and send them upstream depends on the repository that each component fetches from (the "Source code repository" in the component settings on Weblate).

### Maintainer's own repository on GitHub (pull request)

These packages are developed in a public repository on GitHub that accepts pull requests, so the translations can be contributed directly via a pull request.
See, for example, [bethatkinson/rpart#76](https://github.com/bethatkinson/rpart/pull/76).

| Package | Weblate components | Upstream | Fork (`translations` branch) | Maintainer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rpart | [C](https://translate.rx.studio/projects/the-r-project-recommended-packages/rpart-c-files/) + [R](https://translate.rx.studio/projects/the-r-project-recommended-packages/rpart-r-files/) | <https://github.com/bethatkinson/rpart> | [r-devel/rpart](https://github.com/r-devel/rpart/tree/translations) | [Beth Atkinson](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rpart) |
| lattice | [R](https://translate.rx.studio/projects/the-r-project-recommended-packages/lattice-r-files/) | <https://github.com/deepayan/lattice> | [r-devel/lattice](https://github.com/r-devel/lattice/tree/translations) | [Deepayan Sarkar](https://cran.r-project.org/package=lattice) |

For these packages, Weblate fetches from the upstream repository, and pushes the translations to the `translations` branch of a fork in the [`r-devel`](https://github.com/r-devel) GitHub organization (the "Fork" column above).
This way, the commits keep the translators as authors.

To open the pull request and to fix problems in the `translations` branch, you need write access to the fork (be a collaborator of the `r-devel/NAME-OF-THE-PACKAGE` repository).
If you don't have it, ask the team to add you, e.g. in the `#translation` channel of the [R Contributors Zulip](https://contributor.r-project.org/zulip.html) or in the tracking issue.

For each round of contributions:

1. Push the translations from Weblate ("Operations" > "Repository maintenance" > "Push").

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## If the push is rejected

If the push from Weblate is rejected with `! [rejected] master -> translations (fetch first)`, the `translations` branch probably changed outside Weblate (e.g. the previous pull request was squashed or rebased when merged).
See [how this was fixed for rpart](https://github.com/r-devel/translations/issues/68#issuecomment-5589588113) for an example.
:::

2. Check that the new commits are in the `translations` branch of the fork on GitHub.

3. Clone the `translations` branch of the fork:

```sh
git clone --branch translations https://github.com/r-devel/NAME-OF-THE-PACKAGE
cd NAME-OF-THE-PACKAGE
git remote add upstream https://github.com/OWNER/NAME-OF-THE-PACKAGE
git fetch upstream
```

Replace `OWNER/NAME-OF-THE-PACKAGE` with the repository in the "Upstream" column (e.g. `bethatkinson/rpart`).

4. Run the [checks](#checking-the-translations) in this folder.
To see the changes compared to upstream, use `git diff upstream/master -- po/` (or the default branch of the upstream repository, if it isn't `master`).

5. If something doesn't follow the [checks](#checking-the-translations) (e.g. a `.po` file with no translated messages), fix it with commits in the `translations` branch, and push them to the fork (see [Fixing problems](#fixing-problems)).

6. Open a pull request from `r-devel/NAME-OF-THE-PACKAGE:translations` to the upstream repository, and check the changes again in its "Files changed" tab.
In the description, summarize the changes by language and thank the translators (see [Listing the translators](#listing-the-translators)).

### Maintainer's own repository on Codeberg (pull request)

This package is developed in a public repository on Codeberg that accepts pull requests.
See, for example, [jaganmn/Matrix#1](https://codeberg.org/jaganmn/Matrix/pulls/1).

| Package | Weblate components | Upstream | Maintainer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Matrix | [C](https://translate.rx.studio/projects/the-r-project-recommended-packages/matrix-c-files/) + [R](https://translate.rx.studio/projects/the-r-project-recommended-packages/matrix-r-files/) | <https://codeberg.org/jaganmn/Matrix> | [Martin Maechler](https://cran.r-project.org/package=Matrix) |
## After acceptance

After the contribution is accepted upstream (e.g. the pull request is merged), you can:

1. TO DO

2. Unlock the components so new contributions can be made, in the Weblate interface ("Operations" > "Repository maintenance" > "Unlock") or with the CLI inside the Docker container, once for each component:

```sh
weblate unlock_translation the-r-project-recommended-packages/NAME-OF-THE-COMPONENT
```

## Decisions

These are decisions discussed by the team, and they can be revisited if needed.

### New source strings (`.pot` and `.po` files)

When a package changes (e.g. new or modified messages), its `.pot` and `.po` files need to be regenerated (e.g. with `tools::update_pkg_po()`), so that these messages show up in Weblate to be translated.
We don't do this for the recommended packages: it is left to each package's maintainer, and Weblate picks up the new source strings on its next fetch from upstream.
So the contributions sent upstream should include only the translations.
See the discussion in [r-devel/translations#69](https://github.com/r-devel/translations/issues/69).
